newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD sale will affect three sectors - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD sale will affect three sectors - paper.

text.p: The privatization of Brazilian state mining giant CVRD will provoke a restructuring of the steel, aluminium and pulp industries given CVRD's participation in these sectors, a newspaper said.
The government hopes to auction a 40 to 45 percent voting stake in CVRD April 29 for 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion) on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange.

For Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim, which is leading one of the two consortia bidding in the auction, the acquisition of CVRD would signify a leading position in the aluminium market and increased market share in the pulp sector, O Globo said.

If Brazil's largest steelmaker CSN, which leads the other consortium, buys the CVRD stake then it would gain a seat on the administration council of four other steel companies including its main competitor, Usiminas, O Globo said.

Analysts said that Votorantim would use CVRD's stakes in the aluminium and pulp sectors to strengthen its own position in those areas, whereas CSN would probably sell-off these businesses and provoke a restructuring in these sectors, O Globo said.
If Votorantim's consortium wins then CSN would be in a delicate situation because main competitor Usiminas would be strengthened, O Globo said.

Usiminas is 18.5-percent-owned by Japan's Nippon Steel Corp, a member of the Votorantim consortium, and a nine-percent stake in CSN held by CVRD would give the consortium a seat on CSN's administration council.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
